title: 30 Days After Debut, Gaining 400,000 Followers: AI Actor Fang Taozi's First Commercial Deal Triggers a 68,200 Yuan Fine
excerpt: The AI virtual actor "Fang Taozi" was involved in false advertising while promoting colored contact lenses, and the operating company was fined more than 68,200
content_html:
The AI virtual actor "Fang Taozi" was involved in false advertising while promoting colored contact lenses, and the operating company was fined more than 68,200 yuan. Recently, the Guangzhou Panyu District Market Supervision Administration issued an administrative penalty against Guangzhou Wode Film and Television Culture Media Co., Ltd.

An investigation showed that the company produced a colored contact lens advertisement for advertiser Anhui Huaxin Enterprise Management Co., Ltd. and published it through the account of the virtual character "Fang Taozi" to promote "NUTNUTLOOK Jieguoli" colored contact lenses. In the video, "Fang Taozi" described the wearing experience with phrases such as "comfortable all day" and "you can blink with peace of mind." Regulators determined that a virtual character does not have real usage experience, and the content constituted fabricated product usage effects, making it false advertising.

In addition, the colored contact lenses involved are Class III medical devices. The company published the advertisement without obtaining the relevant advertising review approval, which also violated relevant provisions of the Advertising Law.

"Fang Taozi" previously gained popularity through the AI short drama "The Girl Who Was Laid Off," gaining more than 400,000 followers within 30 days of debut. This colored contact lens advertisement was its first commercial collaboration, with a previously announced video quote of 168,000 to 258,000 yuan. The advertisement was taken down shortly after it went live, and regulators subsequently intervened. In September this year, the operator responded that it had declined all business collaborations and would shift its focus to content creation.

This penalty also reflects that the participation of virtual humans in commercial promotion does not mean they can evade advertising regulation. When special products such as medical devices are involved, the advertising content, endorsing subject, and review procedures must all comply with relevant legal requirements.
